surface: google.fr and YouTube signed-out cookie banner
before_observation: Accept required one action while reject required at least five actions through Customize and three settings
after_observation: Equal first-screen Reject all and Accept all buttons each required one click
change_reason: Google explicitly attributed the redesign to updated regulatory guidance and specific CNIL direction
limitations: The after state is documented by Google during rollout rather than an independent preserved browser trace

before_observation: The first layer allowed immediate acceptance but did not offer refusal with equivalent simplicity and a December update remained insufficient
after_observation: Changes deployed from late February offered refusal with simplicity equivalent to acceptance and CNIL found the injunction satisfied
change_reason: The change was submitted within the three-month CNIL injunction and independently rechecked by CNIL
limitations: The public after decision redacts the company name after the statutory publication period but links the same case numbers

before_observation: Accept required one action while reject required at least three actions through settings
after_observation: A first-layer Tout refuser button was added
change_reason: The change occurred during the CNIL investigation before the later sanction decision
limitations: The official decision still found cookie-purpose information insufficient so this is an effort improvement rather than complete compliance

before_observation: Previously placed cookies continued to be read after the user withdrew consent
after_observation: Orange removed first-party cookies and stopped new requests to third-party domains so no further read or write occurred on orange.fr
change_reason: Orange implemented the technical change in response to a CNIL injunction and CNIL closed the order after reviewing evidence
limitations: Third-party cookies could remain in the browser and partner activity outside orange.fr was outside Orange's direct technical control

surface: vanityfair.fr cookie banner and refusal behavior
before_observation: Proceedings following a September 2021 compliance order were closed in July 2022
after_observation: Later checks found consent-required cookies before choice plus continued read and write after Reject all or withdrawal
change_reason: The later failure was found after an earlier compliance proceeding had closed but the source does not establish why the system deteriorated
limitations: Functional refusal effectiveness regressed; later information defects are documented but the earlier state does not provide a comparable transparency baseline

surface: shein.com cookie banner refusal and withdrawal behavior
before_observation: CNIL recorded consent-required cookies before choice plus new reads or writes after Refuse All and after withdrawal
after_observation: The restricted committee recorded that the company ended the refusal infringement and brought withdrawal behavior into conformity during the proceedings
change_reason: The remediation was documented during the CNIL proceedings and the committee therefore found no compliance order necessary
limitations: The public decision does not give the exact deployment date or implementation details and the after state is a regulator case record rather than an independently preserved browser trace
